H639.d: properly, the nose or nostril; hence, the face, and occasionally a person; also (from the rapid breathing in passion) ire

H637.d: meaning accession (used as an adverb or conjunction); also or yea; adversatively though

H622.d: to gather for any purpose; hence, to receive, take away, i.e. remove (destroy, leave behind, put up, restore, etc.)

H699.d: a lattice; (by implication) a window, dovecot (because of the pigeon-holes), chimney (with its apertures for smoke), sluice (with openings for water)

H645.d: strictly a demonstrative particle, here; but used of time, now or then

H680.d: properly, to join; used only as a denominative from H681 (אֵצֶל); to separate; hence, to select, refuse, contract

fb: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
A chieftain of Seir, named in Edom's early lists of clan heads.

H631.d: to yoke or hitch; by analogy, to fasten in any sense, to join battle

fb: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
Pharaoh gave her to Joseph as his wife. She was the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, and she bore him Manasseh and Ephraim, the ancestors of two tribes of Israel.

H669.d: Ephrajim, a son of Joseph; also the tribe descended from him, and its territory
fb: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs

Joseph's younger son. When Jacob blessed the two boys he crossed his hands on purpose and gave Ephraim the bigger blessing over Manasseh. The tribe came to dominate the north so much that the prophets use Ephraim for the whole northern kingdom.
Named twice, in 2 Samuel and John, and nowhere else.

H675.d: Etsbon, the name of two Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the wilderness years.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
A son of Gad who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family. Numbers calls him Ozni.

H692.d: Areli (or an Arelite, collectively), an Israelite and his descendants
fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
He went down to Egypt with Jacob among the seventy, a son of Gad, and his clan, the Arelites, was counted again in the wilderness census.

H656.g: it has come to an end

H617.d: Assir, the name of two Israelites
fb: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1 Chronicles names him twice, and he is a Levite from the wilderness years.
Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
A descendant of Korah, in the Levite line at Exodus 6:24 and 1 Chronicles 6:22.

H676.d: something to sieze with, i.e. a finger; by analogy, a toe

H614.d: gathered, i.e. (abstractly) a gathering in of crops

H646.d: a girdle; specifically the ephod or highpriest's shoulder-piece; also generally, an image

H642.d: a girding on (of the ephod); hence, generally, a plating (of metal)

H601.d: an unclean bird, perhaps the parrot (from its irascibility)

H604.d: some kind of lizard, probably the gecko (from its wail)

H628.d: gathered up together, i.e. a promiscuous assemblage (of people)

H657.d: cessation, i.e. an end (especially of the earth); often used adverb, no further; also the ankle (in the dual), as being the extremity of the leg or foot

H685.d: properly, a step-chain; by analogy, a bracelet

fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Father of Hanniel, Manasseh's leader in dividing Canaan. Nothing else is recorded of him, and he has nothing to do with the priest's garment.

H663.d: Aphek (or Aphik), the name of three places in Palestine
fb: The Philistines captured the ark of the covenant from Israel at Aphek. A later battle there went the other way, when Israel beat the Arameans after Elisha promised King Jehoash the victory.
Two battles happened here. The Philistines took the ark from Israel at Aphek, and later Israel beat the Arameans here, exactly as Elisha had said.
2 Kings names him once, and nothing else is recorded.
A town near Hebron in Judah's hill country, likely home to Paarai the Arbite of David's mighty warriors. It is generally identified with the ruin of er-Rabiyeh, south of Hebron.
A town in Judah's hill country, not one of the several places called Aphek even though the names share a root. Its site is unknown.
Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
Someone of the tribe of Ephraim. In Judges 12 the men of Gilead caught Ephraimites at the fords by making them say shibboleth, and killed those who could not get the first sound right.
Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Ruth and 1 Samuel name him twice, and she is a woman from the wilderness years.

H612.d: a bond (especially manacles of a prisoner)

fb: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
One of Saul's ancestors, named in the opening line of his genealogy and nowhere else.
The Philistines camped here in the Valley of Elah when Goliath came out and David killed him. Chronicles calls it Pas-dammim, and it is generally placed near Socoh in the Shephelah.

H605.d: to be frail, feeble, or (figuratively) melancholy

H650.d: properly, containing, i.e. a tube; also a bed or valley of a stream; also a strong thing or a hero

H609.d: Asa, the name of a king and of a Levite
fb: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

King of Judah for forty-one years, and a real reformer. He removed his own grandmother as queen mother over an obscene idol and drove the male shrine prostitutes out. Early on he trusted God against a huge Cushite invasion, but late in life he hired a foreign king against northern Israel instead.
Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a Levite from the exile and the return.

H623.d: Asaph, the name of three Israelites, and of the family of the first
fb: Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy

A Levite David put in charge of one of the temple choirs. Twelve psalms carry his name, Psalm 50 and Psalms 73 to 83, which means either he wrote them or a guild of musicians kept his name for generations.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
Not David's singer. This Asaph is the one in 2 Kings 18:18 and Isaiah 36:3, and nothing else about him is recorded here.
Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
One of 4 men called Asaph. This one is a Levite from the exile and the return, named twice in 1 Chronicles and Nehemiah.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A man from the exile and the return, and Nehemiah is the only book that names him.
King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

Sennacherib was murdered and Esarhaddon took the Assyrian throne after him. He carried Manasseh of Judah off to Babylon, and his own inscriptions list Manasseh among the vassal kings paying him tribute.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
Shaphan's father. Shaphan was the royal scribe who read the newly found Book of the Law to King Josiah.

H684.d: Otsem, the name of two Israelites
fb: David's brother living at the time of United Monarchy
David's older brother, the sixth of Jesse's sons (1 Chronicles 2:15).
Man living at the time of United Monarchy
A son of Jerahmeel in Judah's genealogy, named once.
Nadab's son, in the Jerahmeelite branch of Judah, and his line ran on through his son Ishi. Nothing further is recorded of him.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
In Jerahmeel's line, the branch of Judah that ran through Jarha, a servant who married into the family.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
Jether's son, and head of an Asherite family. Nothing else is recorded about him.

H682.d: Atsel, the name of an Israelite, and of a place in Palestine
fb: Zechariah says that when the Mount of Olives splits in two, the valley will run as far as Azal. The same name, as Azel, belongs to a Benjamite descendant of Saul through Jonathan, listed with his six sons in Chronicles.

H624.d: collected (only in the plural), i.e. a collection of offerings

fb: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
His descendants were temple servants, Nethinim, who came back from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel.

H671.d: an Apharsekite or Apharsathkite, an unknown Assyrian tribe
H671.g: an Apharsekite or Apharsathkite, an unknown Assyrian tribe
fb: Word sometimes translated as a title
One of the peoples Assyria and Babylon moved into Samaria after deporting Israel. They turn up in Ezra among the officials writing to the king.

H670.d: an Apherasite or inhabitant of an unknown region of Assyria
H670.g: an Apherasite or inhabitant of an unknown region of Assyria
fb: One of the peoples the Assyrians had resettled in Samaria. They wrote with the Dinaites, Elamites and others to the Persian king to stop Jerusalem being rebuilt.
King living at the time of Exile and Return

Identified with Ashurbanipal, the last powerful king of the Neo-Assyrian Empire, who resettled conquered peoples in Samaria. The opponents of the Jews name him in their letter asking the Persian king to stop Jerusalem being rebuilt. His library at Nineveh held thousands of tablets, the Epic of Gilgamesh among them.
Woman living at the time of Exile and Return

An orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai in Susa, she became queen when Ahasuerus put away his first wife. When Haman plotted to wipe out the Jews she went to the king uninvited, at the risk of her life, and Haman ended on his own gallows. The book never names God, and Purim still keeps the day.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Another of Haman's ten sons, killed after Haman's plot against the Jews fell apart.

H660.d: an asp or other venomous serpent

H627.d: a collection of (learned) men (only in the plural)

H688.d: burning, i.e. a carbuncle or other fiery gem

H679.d: a joint of the hand (i.e. knuckle); also (according to some) a party-wall (Ezekiel 41:8)
